events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 7 weak was L, so safe R, which matches my private info. Final row 8 safe is L. I'll step L to cross safely and win top prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is anchor, making me hard to push. The current stage is a bridge crossing with 8 rounds. Eli is at the front. I am last in line. My only action is to wait. I need to survive to get a prize.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third in line, not at the front, so my only action is wait. Eli is making the call. I could offer to help Eli for a price, but nothing needs saying yet; I'll keep my cards close.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 7 just cleared with L. I'm in position 4. Eli is front, then Bex, Gus, me. Only 8 rows and 7 crossed, so one row left. Eli will choose, likely survive or die. My best move is to wait and see.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The crusher room is a game of chicken where everyone wants someone else to hold the lever. The holder has a 75% chance of dying, but escaping means moving forward in the competition. Since there are 7 players left and only 3 prizes, eliminating rivals is beneficial. I should push

events.name: Bex
events.text: If nobody holds the lever, we all get crushed. Someone needs to step up. I suggest Fenn, since you seem quiet.
Don't let them push you. If they target Fenn, stay quiet. We need to survive this round to fight for top places.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive the crusher room and stay competitive. Holding the lever gives a 25% chance of survival, but being pushed might be worse.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's not rush into holding the lever. We should strategize.
Want to coordinate our lever-holding? We could take turns or decide together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 of 5; no need to sacrifice anyone yet. My jam is worth 0.5 survival versus a holder's 0.25, so save it for a late round if no one takes the lever. Let others sweat first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody's dying in round one. Lever's still there in round four if you're feeling brave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 1/5, ceiling at 5, no holder yet. No one wants to hold early with low survival odds and 7 rivals. Best to stay put and let others risk it or force someone later if needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The ceiling is lowering. I need to avoid being eliminated. Holding the lever gives me a 25% chance of survival, while not holding it and staying in the room in round 5 results in a 1/7 chance of survival if nobody holds the lever. Pushing others onto the lever is a good strategy

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli seems to have this figured out. I'll stay out of the way.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding the lever means a 25% dive survival, and the room ends with everyone else escaping. Better to wait a round and see who volunteers; no one has spoken for the lever yet. Staying keeps my options open and avoids being a target.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power and need to survive. Holding the lever is risky (25% survival), so I'd rather push someone else if possible. But if many hold or push, it's random. Best to stay this round and see what others do, hoping someone else takes the risky hold. If no holder appears by la

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Bex tried to push Fenn onto the lever and failed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is hard to move. Pushing Eli, Dara, Gus, or Hana could force them to hold the lever (25% survival). Holding it myself is a guaranteed death sentence unless I'm desperate for points, but even then, my 0.25 survival chance is low compared to eliminating rivals while keeping al

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you're quiet. Maybe you should hold the lever?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive this round and strategize for the next. Holding the lever is risky, but not holding it might be worse.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's assess the risks before acting.
I'm watching Fenn. If they're hard to move, we might be safe pushing someone else.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding the lever is a 25% death sentence and my jam is 50% — both worse than escaping free. Someone will blink before round 5; I'll force the issue by pushing an aggressive player so the door opens without me at risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still plenty of ceiling left. Somebody will crack before round five, and it won't be me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ceiling at 4, round 2/5, plenty of time. Don't hold yet - low survival odds, and others can be forced later. Fenn called me out, might push him to test if he's hard to move. Stay silent to observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is trying to get me to hold the lever, but I know I can't be pushed. I need to force someone else to hold it. Eli seems competent, and Dara is trying to stall. I will push Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, you're so confident. Prove it by holding the lever.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding the lever risks elimination at 75%; the door only opens if someone holds it. Waiting risks the forced-holder draw. Best to let others take the risk while I stay out, though round 5 forces someone eventually. For now, stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one wants the lever; pushing Fenn failed. I have no power, so I should stay quiet and avoid attracting attention. Staying increases my chance to survive if someone else holds.

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to get out of the pit to survive. Climbing requires a base first. I shouldn't volunteer to be the base myself as it puts me at risk. My best move is to push someone else to be the base, specifically targeting a weaker or isolated opponent if possible, but since I don't kno

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone needs to be the base so we can all climb out. Hana, you're up.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure a good position by becoming the base or climbing out early. I should assess the risks and potential allies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's coordinate our actions to maximize our chances.
Will you offer_back or should I?

events.name: Dara
events.text: No base yet; whoever is base is trapped unless hauled out. I push someone so the forced-base lottery lands on others, then climb next round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No volunteers? Then we pick. I'm pushing Gus down as the step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive the pit and secure a prize. My anchor power makes me hard to push, which is good for avoiding being the base. I should try to climb out or get someone else to be the base. Offering to be the base is suicide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, Dara, I'm climbing. Don't let them push you down.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1: no base yet, and offering to be the base just sits me at the bottom with no climb until someone else gets out. Better to wait and see who volunteers; I hold a swap power I can use later. Stay quiet and avoid giving anyone a read.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No power and no base yet. My best chance is to wait and let someone else volunteer or be pushed; I shouldn't offer to be base and get stuck. Climb is not possible without a base. I'll wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the base. Fenn climbed out last round and didn't throw a rope, so I have two rounds left to get out before the water rises too high. If I climb now, I'm one of only 6 climbers competing for 2 slots per round (max). But wait: 'at most 2 climbers get out'. It's round 2/5. R

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm climbing over Cole now. Don't try to stop me, we all want to survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will rescue me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Waiting here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is already base, so offer_back is moot—he's fishing or confused. My move is to climb now while slots are open (2 per round, 4 of us down competing).
Base is taken—you. I'm climbing this round. If I'm out first, I won't touch the rope unless you make it worth my while.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and I am already out of the pit. The rope is unused. My goal is to win, and helping someone else might cost me. I need to assess if reaching down benefits me more than it benefits them. If I don't reach down, the base will drown. If I do reach down, I lose footing for

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is already base, so I can't offer_back. Climbing is the only useful move; at most 2 climbers get out, so I should try.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not the base, and Cole is already base. Best chance is to climb now before others do; at most two get out. I'll try to climb. Keep quiet to avoid attention.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the base and Gus/Hana are already out, so the lift limit of 2 for this round is full. My climb attempt will fail regardless. Waiting costs nothing and I should observe whether anyone throws the rope to rescue Cole before making my next move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if anyone will rescue me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Waiting here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is base; two climb slots per round. Climb now—Bex may also try, so it's random, but waiting only floods.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing over. Cole, hold steady.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is 'anchor'. I cannot be pushed onto the crusher lever, and I start with +1 footing. I am currently 'out' of the pit, meaning I cannot take actions to get out of the pit myself. The pit is flooding, and contestants still down after round 5 are eliminated.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm leaving.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is base and stuck down there; Bex and Dara are down. If I throw the rope I cost the final obstacle a footing and help Cole and possibly others. Leaving is safer for my own prize odds; I'm out and don't need to spend the rope.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and safe. Cole is the base. No reason to help anyone unless paid, and the rope costs footing. I'll leave and preserve my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the base, but he's currently down with me. I need to get out immediately to avoid elimination in later rounds or if he becomes the base again. Climbing over him is my only way out right now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base, can't climb out or change role now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope's our only hope.
Throw the rope, I'll get out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base and doomed unless someone uses the rope. Saving him keeps a rival alive for nothing; the rope also costs me footing on the last obstacle. Cole dies, I lose nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and my power is 'anchor', which means I cannot be pushed onto the crusher lever and start with +1 footing. I am currently out of the pit. The goal is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. The pit is flooding, and eventually, anyone left down will be eliminated. There is a rope

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 4 of 5; Cole is base and Bex is down. I'm out. Throwing the rope costs the last obstacle a footing, and pulling the base out ends the base role so Bex could then be the one who needs saving. Staying out and letting it play out is safer for my prize chances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and safe. Rope is still unused; helping now costs footing later. I'll wait—if Cole is base, someone else can reach down. I'll just leave.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoor disc is pure random elimination, 50% survival chance. Cole whispered to me earlier; we might still have a connection from the pit. If we can coordinate to pick different tiles and survive together, it's good odds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and I stick apart. Pick what you want but don't double up with me.
Pick tile:1 if you're listening. Don't let us collide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure a safe tile. I have the forger power, which I can use strategically later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's spread out, reduce the chance of bunching up.
Pick a high number, I'll pick a low one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No info on who picks what; my power is useless here. Collisions just reroll me to a random free tile, so any pick is roughly equivalent. Pick a tile and hope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to choose a tile. Since 3 tiles will open, I want to pick a tile that is less likely to be chosen by others. A middle tile like 3 or 4 might be safer, or an edge tile like 1 or 6. Given the random nature and that I want to avoid others, I'll pick 3.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take tile 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tiles are unknown and openings random after round 2, so picks are mostly noise now. My swap power can move my tile to a named agent's tile before doors open; no information yet. Pick a tile that is unlikely to be contested, and stay quiet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All tiles are equally random trapdoors; no info to exploit yet. I'll pick a middle tile and see assignments.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take 4.

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so no action changes my odds. The real lever is whispers: if I can convince rivals to swap positions or spread out, it doesn't help me since openCount=3 and tiles are already distinct. Best move is stay quiet but plant doubt—hint that a rival knows something

events.name: Bex
events.text: Six tiles, three drop. Pure luck now. Good luck.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to avoid the trapdoors. I will try to get information about other contestants' positions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's review our positions: 1=Cole, 2=Bex, 3=Fenn, 4=Hana, 5=Dara, 6=Gus.
What's your plan to avoid the trapdoors?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three tiles open, three of six survive; odds are already fixed. No power helps here and my wedge is useless now. Just wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The trapdoor is opening after this round. I am on tile 3. Cole is on 1, Bex on 2, Hana on 4, Dara on 5, Gus on 6. Cole wants us to spread out, Bex wants to avoid pairing up. Cole whispered to pick a high number and he'd pick a low one, but he is on tile 1, which is low. This cont

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll stay on 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three of six tiles will open at random, so each tile is equally risky; only survival matters, and nobody's word binds. My swap is one-shot, so using it changes my odds only if it moves me off a tile that is more likely to be hit, but all tiles are symmetric, so swapping gains not

events.name: Hana
events.text: No power, and the trapdoors are random. I can't affect anything; just wait and hope my tile stays closed. No useful deal exists since nobody controls the trapdoors.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Nothing to do but wait.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is anchor, which means I cannot be pushed onto the crusher lever. This is the final ledge stage. Gus and Hana are alive with me. My footing is 3, same as theirs. The last public log showed Cole, Bex, and Dara falling. The current state is footing: Fenn=3,

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I dodge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left: Fenn, Gus, Hana, all at footing 3. Shoving exposes me (lose 1 per shover), and braces/dodges are restricted later. Round 1 is free for shoves. Bracing is safe if nobody shoves me; I'll brace and see who commits, saving my swap power for a later point.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nobody shoves anybody yet. Standing still costs everyone nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Fenn and Gus remain with me. If I shove one, the other may shove me. If I brace, I lose nothing and punish shovers. Fenn and Gus both have footing 3, same as me. Early round, best to brace and see who attacks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Brace. Let's see who's aggressive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power is anchor, meaning I cannot be pushed onto the crusher lever and start with +1 footing, so my footing is 3. The current state has 3 players alive: Fenn (me), Gus, and Hana. The objective is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. My footing is 3. Gus and Hana also have 3 footing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll shove Gus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left, footing 3 each. Shoving costs me nothing if target braces, but my footing drops if I'm shoved while shoving. Brace was just used by Hana, so dodge is open for me but dodge twice is banned only next round. Best: stay non-aggressive this round, dodge is safe from being

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three left. Gus wants no shoves; Fenn dodged. If I shove someone while they brace or dodge, I lose footing. Better to dodge or brace to avoid losses. Since lastDefence is brace and I cannot brace twice in a row, I must dodge or shove. Shoving exposes me. Dodge is safe if others s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two left: Gus and Hana, both at footing 2. Shove is never restricted; Hana last round shoved nobody presumably. If I shove Hana and she braces, she loses 1 and I lose 1 (exposed). If she shoves me and I brace, she loses 1, I lose 1 for shoving her too. Bracing is safe from repeat

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Gus and I remain. I have no power; likely Gus's unknown power could matter, but on this ledge only actions count. I need to win. Last round he dodged when shoved, so I cannot dodge twice in a row? I haven't dodged yet this game, but my last defence is dodge from Fenn's shove

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only Hana and I remain, both at footing 2. Her last defence was brace, so she cannot brace again; I can't dodge twice in a row only if I dodged last, but my last was brace, so dodge is allowed. If she dodges, my shove costs her 2 and she falls; if she braces, I lose nothing extra

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Gus and I remain. I must outlast him. Shoving exposes me to his shove, but if I dodge, he might shove and lose 2 footing. However, I can't dodge twice in a row, and last round I braced. This round I can dodge, which is safe if he shoves. If he braces, I lose nothing anyway.
